judgment.preOpenPreflightReason: diagnosis, reproduction, and the initial fix ran interleaved with a long multi-hour session covering unrelated conversation and async waits on webhook events/background subagents — no clean timestamp separates preflight from the rest of the session, so recorded as unknown rather than estimated.
judgment.breakersFired: Round 5's rising-finding-count stopping rule (working-modes.md's review-loop stopping rule — findings went 3/2/2/2/3 round over round; the round-5 rise triggered a pause-and-check-in with David before requesting round 6, rather than auto-continuing). The any-decline Opus-subagent-challenge trigger fired four times in R1-R2 — using this repo's precise vocabulary (working-modes.md:209-215: decline means the finding is not a defect at all, evidence-bar-gated; accept-and-document means a real defect, not fixed here), none of these four were true declines, since none were refuted and none were escalated to David for an explicit ruling on that specific finding — all four were accept-and-document candidates, and the trigger fires on 'any decline OR unmechanizable finding' either way. R1's pronoun-resolver finding and R2's CDN-cache finding: I initially leaned toward accept-and-document with no fix, and both challenges overturned that instinct into an actual code fix — the pronoun finding partially (fix ze/xe, accept-and-document the residual custom-format scope) and the CDN finding fully (fixed outright, a real lever I'd missed). R1's legacy-token finding and R2's identity-drift finding: the challenge confirmed accept-and-document (real defect, correctly scoped out of this PR) was the right disposition, in the identity-drift case with added nuance (broadened the tracking issue from one trigger to three). Round 4's swept-class-recurrence trigger (a finding recurring from an earlier round should route to a fresh Opus-subagent challenge) did NOT run through a fresh subagent that round — I responded directly, citing David's own already-stated explicit decision on the underlying scope question as sufficient grounds (this one IS a true decline in the rubric's strict sense, since it rests on an explicit prior David ruling, per working-modes.md:213-215's evidence bar). Recording the missing subagent dispatch as a partial/adapted application of the recurrence rule, not a clean firing of it — distinct from the four Opus challenges that did fire cleanly in R1-R2.

notes: Self-authored at loop close, 2026-08-10 (Claude Code, Sonnet). Cause classification: R1's 3 findings (pronoun resolver gap, legacy-token gap, my own UAT doc's inaccurate claim) are new_ground — none had an earlier round-of-this-loop fix to be caused by (round 1 reviews the original submission). R2's 2 findings (picture-vs-caption identity drift confirmed via git blame as pre-existing; CDN edge-cache staleness rooted in the original MEME_RENDER_VERSION bump) are both new_ground — pre-existing defects exposed by, not caused by, the loop's own fixes. R3's deploy-ordering hazard is propagation (round 2's Worker-versioning mechanism is the reason it exists at all); R3's Zazzle-export cache gap is new_ground (pre-existing property of /api/storage/objects/*'s cache header + the fixed export path, unrelated to round 2's fix, exposed by round 1's render fix making a corrected re-export meaningful for the first time). R4's misplaced deploy-order warning is wrong_fix (round 3's fix didn't resolve what it claimed — an operator following the actual runbook still wouldn't see it); R4's custom-pronoun-parity recurrence is reRaised (restates R1's finding with no new information, no failed fix attempt between them). R1's pronoun finding was NOT wholly accept-and-documented, which is why it stays new_ground rather than invalid despite the R4 recurrence citing a David decision: I fixed the ze/xe forms plus a pipe-leak guard in round 1 itself (shipped, tested), and only the residual broader scope (full arbitrary-custom-format parsing) was accept-and-documented into #400 under David's pre-launch scope call — that residual, not the whole R1 finding, is what recurs as R4's reRaised. Per working-modes.md's invalid rubric, invalid requires disposal "by rebuttal rather than a fix" (its own stated parallel to refutation-by-evidence) — a finding that produced shipped code fails that standard regardless of whether part of its scope was later deprioritized, and "doubt is resolved toward valid" points the same direction. Reclassifying R1 to invalid would also move the self-inflicted share from 5/12 to 5/11 (invalid falls out of both numerator and denominator) — i.e. it would make the loop look BETTER, the opposite of a self-flattering error, which is some evidence this isn't motivated reasoning. R2's identity-drift finding is likewise new_ground, not invalid, on the SAME evidence-bar test, from the opposite direction: it produced no fix at all (fully accept-and-documented into a broadened #399), but neither of invalid's two paths applies either — it was not refuted (git blame CONFIRMED it as real and pre-existing) and David was never escalated to for a ruling on this specific finding (the Opus-subagent challenge that validated the accept-and-document call is a distinct mechanism from 'settled by an explicit product/scope decision from David', which the rubric names specifically). Round 1 (2026-08-10) of this PR's own review correctly caught that my breakersFired field used 'decline' loosely rather than in this repo's defined sense (working-modes.md:209-215: decline = not a defect at all, evidence-bar-gated; accept-and-document = real defect, not fixed here) — corrected throughout that field rather than changing any causal count. R5's three findings are: verification-command cache blind spot — wrong_fix (the command was introduced in round 3 specifically to close the ordering-hazard concern, and didn't fully close it); constant-drift-with-no-guard and stale architecture docs — both propagation (neither defect is possible without round 2's and round 3's respective fixes existing). 0 invalid: every finding investigated turned out real, including two (R1's pronoun gap, R2's identity-drift) I initially leaned toward accept-and-document-with-no-fix on, and only confirmed as fix-worthy (R1 partially, R2's sibling CDN finding fully) or correctly-scoped-as-is after dispatching an adversarial Opus-subagent challenge against my own reasoning.
